record.paper_title: From P systems to morphogenetic systems: an overview and open problems
record.original_question: Do there exist morphogenetic systems that are computationally universal in the Turing sense and at the same time self-healing for injuries of degree strictly greater than 1, where the degree of an injury is the graph-theoretic distance between the pre-injury and post-injury configurations in the configuration digraph?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4 Are there Turing-universal M systems which are simultaneously self-healing of a degree greater than 1?

Definition 6 [18] An injury to a morphogenetic system M is a transition of the system given by a pair of configurations (x, y) such that y cannot be obtained from x by any one step of the system M. The degree of the injury is the undirected graph-theoretic distance between x and y in the configuration digraph.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A morphogenetic system (M system) is an abstract computational model whose configurations are finite arrangements of abstract tiles in a discrete d-dimensional space, evolving by a fixed set of local rewriting/assembly rules. The set of all reachable configurations together with the one-step transition relation forms the configuration digraph of the system, whose vertices are configurations and whose directed edges are one-step transitions.

An injury to such a system M is a pair (x, y) of configurations where y cannot be reached from x in a single legitimate step of M. The degree of the injury (x, y) is defined as the graph-theoretic distance between x and y in the underlying undirected graph of the configuration digraph.

The system M is called self-healing of degree k if, after any injury (x, y) with degree at most k that occurs during a computation, M is still able to continue and complete its intended computation correctly (i.e., reach the same final result it would have reached without the injury).

The system M is called Turing-universal if it can simulate the computation of an arbitrary Turing machine on arbitrary input.

Question: Does there exist a morphogenetic system M that is simultaneously
(i) Turing-universal, and
(ii) self-healing of degree strictly greater than 1?
artifact.status_search_result: Existing literature establishes Turing-universal M systems that are self-healing of degree 1, but no construction or impossibility result has been reported for degree strictly greater than 1. The question therefore appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Self-healing Turing-universal computation in morphogenetic systems
status_evidence.snippet: A Turing universal string acceptor M system with self-healing capabilities of degree 1 is presented.
status_evidence.claim: Only degree-1 self-healing universal M systems have been constructed in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Morphogenetic computing: computability and complexity results
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of computability results for M systems; degree-1 self-healing universal constructions discussed, higher-degree case not resolved.
status_evidence.claim: Higher-degree self-healing universality is not addressed as resolved.
